lead.label: 11c
lead.why: Abstract: '11c (IC50 = 22.7 and 29.2 uM) and 11f (IC50 = 28.7 and 16.9 uM) were the most potent among all compounds against both PC-3 and MCF-7 respectively'. The abstract names TWO co-leads (11c best on PC-3, 11f best on MCF-7; both used for docking and the topo I assay); 11c, named first, was transcribed. 11f uses identical chemistry with 4-methylphenyl isothiocyanate.

reactions.conditions: aqueous KOH / EtOH, reflux 3 h (thiourea formation), then conc. HCl, reflux 2 h (cyclisation); 95%
reactions.source: Section 2.1.1 General procedure (9a-b); Scheme 1 step a

reactions.conditions: Mannich reaction: EtOH, reflux 5-8 h; column chromatography; 83%
reactions.source: Section 2.1.2 General procedure (10a-f), entry 10c; Scheme 1 step b

reactions.conditions: ethanolic KOH (2%, 1.1 equiv), MeI (1.2 equiv), rt, 12 h; column chromatography; 71%
reactions.source: Section 2.1.3 General procedure (11a-f), entry 11c; Scheme 1 step c

notes: Co-lead 11f (2-methylthio-5-methyl-5-(piperidinomethyl)-3-(p-tolyl)-4-imidazolidinone) is the same 3-step route from DL-alanine and p-tolyl isothiocyanate (via 9b, 10f). 11c is racemic (DL-alanine, no stereo). The S-methylation gives the 2-(methylthio)-imidazol-4-one tautomer (C2=N1, 13C 160.4 C=N, 183.4 C=O, 74.3 quaternary C5), so the SMILES has C2=N1; the title/name calls it '4-imidazolidinone' loosely. Paper uses reagents 'purchased from Aldrich'; no explicit statement for piperidine specifically. 9a text has an inconsistent MS value (not relevant).
